tool_output.scenario_name: Legacy Cancellation Update After Backfill Batch
tool_output.description: A legacy cancellation updates only the text status to refunded after that row has already been processed by the backfill. The new status_id identifier remains stale as pending.

phases.name: Seed Phase
phases.description: Initial database state with orders table

phases.name: Expand Schema
phases.description: Add order_statuses lookup and status_id FK

expand_schema.description: DDL: Create order_statuses lookup table and add orders.status_id column

backfill_orders.description: DML: Backfill orders.status_id from orders.status based on order_statuses lookup

legacy_order_cancel_refund.description: Legacy Application: Cancel/refund order by updating orders.status = 'refunded' directly

legacy_order_mark_shipped.description: Legacy Application: Mark order as shipped by updating orders.status = 'shipped'

new_app_read_status.description: New Application: Read status from status_id via order_statuses join

invariants.name: Status Consistency Invariant
invariants.description: Whenever orders.status_id is populated, it must match orders.status text exactly.

permitted_repairs.name: Install Sync Trigger Before Backfill
permitted_repairs.description: Ensure any direct legacy status update propagates to status_id immediately.

tool_input.hypothesis: If the backfill runs and populates the status_id column, and subsequently a legacy application update modifies the legacy status text directly without updating the status_id, the status_id and status text will diverge, violating the Status Consistency Invariant.
tool_input.reason: This sequence tests whether a legacy write occurring after the backfill has processed a row causes a stale status_id to persist, leading to an inconsistent state.
